title: TIGIT and PD-1 co-inhibition in exhausted T cells
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. TIGIT and PD-1 can be co-expressed on dysfunctional tumor-infiltrating T cells. Blocking both pathways may restore effector activity more strongly than either blockade alone when CD226 signaling remains intact. Candidate response markers include PD-L1 expression, TIGIT-positive CD8 T cells, CD226 availability, and an inflamed interferon-gamma transcriptional program.

title: Role of the PVR-CD226-TIGIT axis in antitumor immunity
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. PVR/CD155 can bind the inhibitory receptor TIGIT and the costimulatory receptor CD226. A tumor with high PVR but low or dysfunctional CD226 may not respond despite abundant TIGIT. Biomarker interpretation should therefore consider receptor balance rather than TIGIT expression alone.

title: Randomized anti-TIGIT plus anti-PD-1 study in PD-L1-selected NSCLC
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. In a hypothetical randomized phase 2 study, the combination showed a higher response rate than anti-PD-1 alone in a PD-L1-enriched population, but confidence intervals were wide and overall-survival follow-up was immature. Exploratory ctDNA clearance correlated with radiographic response. This record is for software testing and must not be treated as clinical evidence.

title: Confirmatory anti-TIGIT combination study with mixed efficacy
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. A hypothetical phase 3 trial did not clearly reproduce the magnitude of benefit suggested by an earlier study. Subgroup analyses were inconclusive, and TIGIT immunohistochemistry lacked a prospectively validated threshold. The result illustrates contradictory evidence and the need to avoid class-wide efficacy claims.

title: Candidate biomarker framework for TIGIT combinations
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. A composite biomarker strategy may be more defensible than a single-analyte marker. Suggested components are tumor PD-L1, immune-cell CD226, PVR/CD155 ligand abundance, an interferon-gamma inflamed signature, and early ctDNA decline. Each component requires assay validation and prospective testing.

title: Potential resistance mechanisms to TIGIT blockade
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING RECORD. Potential resistance contexts include low CD226, immune-excluded tumors, weak antigen presentation, and oncogenic states associated with non-inflamed microenvironments. STK11 or KEAP1 alterations may be useful stratification variables, but they are not established TIGIT-specific exclusion biomarkers.
